Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- Failing test and symptom:
  - The test org.apache.commons.codec.binary.Base64InputStreamTest.testCodec101() creates a Base64InputStream over a ByteArrayInputStream containing Base64TestData.CODEC_101_MULTIPLE_OF_3, then performs a single in.read(result) and asserts the returned count c > 0.
  - The failure indicates that the first read returned 0.

- Relevant bug report:
  - “Base64InputStream#read(byte[]) incorrectly returns 0 at end of any stream which is multiple of 3 bytes long”
  - This manifests in higher-level readers like InputStreamReader as “Underlying input stream returned zero bytes”, because InputStream.read(byte[]) returning 0 (when len > 0) violates the expected behavior unless no bytes were requested.

- Code path in Base64InputStream:
  - Base64InputStream.read(b, offset, len) (lines 138–180) validates arguments, then:
    - If base64.hasData() is false, it reads from the underlying InputStream into a temporary buffer (lines 164–176), possibly sets the Base64 codec’s initial output buffer to the caller’s array for direct fill (lines 169–171), and calls either base64.encode(...) or base64.decode(...).
    - It then immediately returns base64.readResults(b, offset, len) (line 178).
  - Base64.readResults(b, bPos, bAvail) (lines 406–423) returns:
    - A positive number if there is buffered data to deliver.
    - -1 if EOF has been reached and there is no buffered data.
    - 0 if there is no buffered data and EOF has not yet been reached (buffer == null and eof == false).

- The problem:
  - The implementation of Base64InputStream.read(byte[], int, int) lacks the retry loop that ensures it does not return 0 when more input can still be read to produce data. There is even an in-method comment explicitly describing the need for such a while-loop to handle the case where Base64.readResults() returns 0 (lines 148–163: “Rationale for while-loop on (readLen == 0)… This is a fix for CODEC-101”), but the actual loop is missing.
  - As written, if base64.readResults(...) returns 0 (no buffered output yet, not at EOF), read(byte[], int, int) simply returns 0 to the caller, violating the InputStream contract and triggering the observed behavior.
  - This can occur at block boundaries where the codec has not yet emitted output (e.g., after consuming input but before producing a decoded/encoded block, particularly with exact multiple-of-3 byte lengths in encode mode or other boundary/alignment cases in decode mode). The test uses data crafted for CODEC-101 (“MULTIPLE_OF_3”), which is precisely the scenario that can yield a transient 0 from Base64.readResults() unless the caller keeps trying.

- Additional corroboration:
  - Base64InputStream.read() (single-byte) implements a protective while loop to avoid returning 0 (lines 108–116: it keeps calling read(singleByte, 0, 1) until r != 0). That inconsistency further highlights the bug: read(byte[], int, int) should do something similar but does not.

- How the failure arises in the test:
  1. testCodec101() constructs a Base64InputStream over the provided data (default constructor => decoding mode).
  2. The first call to read(result) reaches Base64InputStream.read(byte[], int, int).
  3. Depending on the boundary conditions of the data (crafted to be a multiple-of-3 case), Base64.decode(...) does not immediately make output available in the internal buffer, so Base64.readResults(...) returns 0 (buffer == null, eof == false).
  4. Because there is no retry loop, read(byte[], int, int) returns 0 to the test.
  5. The assertion assertTrue("Codec101: First read successful [c=" + c + "]", c > 0) fails.

- Root cause:
  - Missing retry loop in Base64InputStream.read(byte[], int, int) to prevent returning 0 when Base64.readResults(...) returns 0 but more data can be read or decoded. The method’s own comment references this loop as the fix for CODEC-101, but it is not implemented in the body, leading to the erroneous 0 return and the test failure.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
